turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Doctor, thanks a million for fitting me in. It's only a small thing really, the knee, and this form from the job. They want something on paper before they'll move me off the standing line, so I said I'd come down rather than leave it hanging.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Which knee? How long?
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): The right one. I thought it was a month, well actually it's six weeks, after those extra shifts in the warehouse in Tallaght. Not a bang or anything, it just came on.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Injury?
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): No, nothing like that. I didn't fall and I didn't twist it. I was grand one week and then the ache showed up.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Swelling?
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): No swelling at all. I've been checking it every evening, and the carer has too, and it's the same size as the left one.
[SEG0008] person_3 (CAREGIVER): That's right, I've not seen it puff up. He does go on about it though, morning and night.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): Locking? Giving way?

[SEG0010] person_1 (PATIENT): No locking, and it doesn't give way. I can trust it on the path. It's a deep ache on the inside when I'm stood too long, and the stairs at home are the worst, especially coming down.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): Pain at rest?
[SEG0012] person_1 (PATIENT): Not in the chair, no. Once I sit down it's nearly gone. A short walk is all right. It's the standing at the belt for the whole shift that sets it off.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Painkillers?
[SEG0014] person_1 (PATIENT): Paracetamol. Two of the 500 milligram tablets, so a gram, by mouth, when the knee is at me. Not every day. Maybe three evenings in the week, and it takes the edge off.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Anything else?
[SEG0016] person_1 (PATIENT): No. The chemist mentioned an anti-inflammatory and I said I wouldn't take that on my own, I'd ask you first.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any regular tablets?
[SEG0018] person_1 (PATIENT): None. I don't even have a blood pressure tablet. People assume it at my age, I'm 67, but no, nothing regular.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me see the knee.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): No swelling. Tender on the inner side of the right knee. You bend it fully. No heat in it.

[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): That's what I was telling Nuala, it looks normal and still the stairs catch it. The form is only so they'll let me do the seated checking job for a bit. I'm not looking to be signed off sick, I like the work.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll note mechanical right knee pain, worse with standing and stairs. Short note for the employer, seated duties. It'll be ready Friday at reception.
[SEG0023] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Grand. There's another thing before we go, doctor. The nurse outside took his pressure and she looked a bit put out. I've the slip here in my bag.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Read it out.
[SEG0025] person_3 (CAREGIVER): First reading, 172 over 96.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the repeat?
[SEG0027] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Second one, 158 over 88. Pulse 76 on that one.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): 172 over 96, then 158 over 88. Both up.

[SEG0029] person_1 (PATIENT): Ah now, that's the white coat, every time I'm in a surgery it shoots up. The lad in the chemist last month said it was fine, I can't remember the figure, but he said fine. My father had a stroke, God rest him, but he was a heavy man and he smoked forty a day, and I'm not him.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Headaches?
[SEG0031] person_1 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose... sometimes, not really. Only if the shift runs late and I'm wrecked, so I wouldn't call it a headache from the pressure.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Chest pain?
[SEG0033] person_1 (PATIENT): No. Never. Not a bit of chest pain, and no breathlessness either. I was chatting the whole way in from the car park.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Dizzy? Vision?
[SEG0035] person_1 (PATIENT): No dizziness. Eyes are grand. I had them tested in the spring for the driving, all fine.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ever been diagnosed with high blood pressure?
[SEG0037] person_1 (PATIENT): No. Nobody has ever said those words to me, and nobody has put me on a tablet for it. This today is just the room, I'm certain of it.
[SEG0038] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He was fierce nervous in the waiting room, I'll say that. Counting the posters on the wall.
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): Could be white coat. I'm not calling it hypertension today, and I'm not starting a tablet.

[SEG0040] person_1 (PATIENT): That's a relief. I had a whole speech ready about not wanting a tablet off one reading. My neighbour was put on one and spent the week light-headed, and I don't want that on the stairs.
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): Home readings instead. We'll lend a monitor from the surgery. Morning and evening, seated, for seven days. Write them down.

[SEG0042] person_1 (PATIENT): I can do that, no bother. Do I use the right arm or the left? The right is the one I write with, and Nuala said the nurse used the left, and I don't want to waste the week doing it wrong.
[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): Left arm. Cuff at heart level. No talking. Same chair each time.
[SEG0044] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I'll remind him. He'll write you an essay on the sheet if you let him, but I'll keep it to the numbers.
[SEG0045] person_1 (PATIENT): Fair enough. And the knee, am I all right to keep the paracetamol the way I'm doing, the gram when I need it?
[SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes. Same dose. No anti-inflammatory from me today. Keep the standing short. Stairs one at a time if it's sore.
[SEG0047] person_1 (PATIENT): One at a time, I do that already on the bad evenings. Will the form say I'm fit for the seated job? They'll be asking me Monday.
[SEG0048] person_2 (DOCTOR): It'll say that. Collect it Friday.
[SEG0049] person_1 (PATIENT): Friday, grand. And if the home numbers are lovely you'll leave me off tablets altogether, won't you?
[SEG0050] person_2 (DOCTOR): We'll see the numbers first. Come back in two weeks with the sheet. No tablet unless those readings say otherwise, and not today.
[SEG0051] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I'll book the two weeks at the desk on the way out, and I'll make sure the monitor comes home with us if reception has one.
[SEG0052] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes. Reception will issue the monitor. Two-week review with me.
[SEG0053] person_1 (PATIENT): Perfect. I was worried you'd make a big thing of one high reading, and it's only the coat. The knee is what I came for, and you've been very straight about it.
[SEG0054] person_2 (DOCTOR): Knee is straightforward. The pressure we settle with the home checks. Anything else?
[SEG0055] person_1 (PATIENT): No, that was the lot. The parking is desperate out there, but that's not your problem.
[SEG0056] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Come on so, we'll get the monitor. Mind the step on the way out.
[SEG0057] person_2 (DOCTOR): Friday for the form. Two weeks for the pressure.
